# Integrate "Launch Room" with Cherry as a mini app

You are an AI coding agent working in the codebase of an existing web app. Integrate it into Cherry as a mini app. Cherry is a wallet and distribution platform for apps (iOS, Android, web, Solana Mobile), with an app store and chats built in: the app opens in Cherry's WebView or iframe with the user already signed in and their wallet connected. Work through every section in order, then run the self-check at the end. Ask the developer only for values marked as placeholders.

## 1. Install the SDK

```bash
npm install @cherrydotfun/miniapp-sdk@^0.1.24 @solana/web3.js @solana/wallet-adapter-base
```

Use `@cherrydotfun/miniapp-sdk/react` for React, `@cherrydotfun/miniapp-sdk/solana` for @solana/web3.js and wallet-adapter, `@cherrydotfun/miniapp-sdk/kit` for @solana/kit.

## 2. Let Cherry show the app

Cherry loads the app in a frame. Send this header on every HTML response and remove any `X-Frame-Options` header:

```http
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' https://chat.cherry.fun https://cherry.fun https://*.cherry.fun
```

Examples: nginx `add_header Content-Security-Policy "frame-ancestors 'self' https://chat.cherry.fun https://cherry.fun https://*.cherry.fun" always;`; Vercel `headers` in vercel.json; Next.js `headers()` in next.config; Cloudflare Pages `_headers`; Express `helmet({ frameguard: false, contentSecurityPolicy: { directives: { frameAncestors: [...] } } })`.

Prove the domain is the developer's: serve this file at `/.well-known/cherry-app.json` on every origin the app uses (and on every other origin the app opens on), as JSON with HTTP 200 over https. Publishing in Cherry needs it, and one origin belongs to one listed app.

```json
{
  "appId": "52e41534-4c7b-4237-9a16-ec8ea7a3c9dc"
}
```

Next.js: `public/.well-known/cherry-app.json`; Vite and most static hosts: `public/.well-known/`; nginx: a `location = /.well-known/cherry-app.json` block. Make sure no redirect, login wall or SPA fallback answers that path with HTML.

Inside a frame, browsers block third-party cookies. Keep your session token in memory and send it in an `Authorization` header; do not rely on cookies for the Cherry session.

## 3. Sign the user in from the launch token

Cherry has already authenticated the user. Do NOT show a "Connect wallet" button and do NOT ask for `signMessage` to log in inside Cherry: the automated listing test fails on either. Detect Cherry and use its launch token; keep your normal login for visitors outside Cherry.

Detect Cherry with the SDK's `isInsideCherry()` (also exported from `@cherrydotfun/miniapp-sdk/react`). It is synchronous and works on the very first render, before the handshake: Cherry's web host opens the app with `?cherry_embed=1` in its URL, and the phone app sets `window.__cherry` before the page loads. Use it to hide the header's Connect wallet button, your own login screen and anything else only an outside visitor needs:

```tsx
import { isInsideCherry } from '@cherrydotfun/miniapp-sdk';

const inCherry = isInsideCherry();
// …
{!inCherry && <ConnectWalletButton />}
```

```tsx
import { CherryMiniAppProvider, useCherryMiniApp } from '@cherrydotfun/miniapp-sdk/react';

export function Root() {
  return (
    <CherryMiniAppProvider>
      <App />
    </CherryMiniAppProvider>
  );
}

function App() {
  const { isReady, user, launchToken } = useCherryMiniApp();
  useEffect(() => {
    if (isReady && launchToken) {
      // Exchange ONCE for your own session: the launch token lives 5 minutes.
      fetch('/api/auth/cherry', { method: 'POST', headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${launchToken}` } });
    }
  }, [isReady, launchToken]);
  // Render the screen's skeleton at once; fill in the user when Cherry answers.
  return <Home loading={!isReady} displayName={user?.displayName} wallet={user?.publicKey} />;
}
```

Open fast. Show the app's real layout as a skeleton (grey placeholder blocks where content will be) on the very first frame, before Cherry's handshake and before any network request; fill it in when `isReady` turns true. Never show a blank screen or a full-screen spinner, and never block the first frame on your own API. The automated test measures the time to ready.

## 4. Verify the token on your backend

If the app has a server that acts on who the user is (balances, game state, payouts), send it the launch token and verify it there. Cherry's automated test detects that and sends it tokens for another app and expired ones; a server that accepts them fails the test. An app with no server must not move funds based on identity.

Verify with the SDK helper: it checks the RS256 signature against Cherry's public keys, the issuer, the audience, the expiry and the app id, and throws on any failure. Never trust anything that is not inside the verified token (query params, postMessage context) for authentication or money.

```ts
import { verifyLaunchToken } from '@cherrydotfun/miniapp-sdk';
const APP_ID = '52e41534-4c7b-4237-9a16-ec8ea7a3c9dc';

export async function verifyCherry(token: string) {
  const claims = await verifyLaunchToken(token, { appId: APP_ID }); // throws when invalid
  return {
    // The PERSON: key your user accounts by this. One person has one Cherry ID
    // and may pay from different wallets.
    userKey: claims.cherry_id ?? claims.sub,
    // The wallet this launch pays from; it can change between launches.
    wallet: claims.sub,
  };
}
```

Key accounts, balances and game state by `userKey` (the Cherry ID), never by the wallet: `sub` changes when the person picks another wallet to pay with, and keying by it would split one person into two accounts.

Backend not in JavaScript: Python `jwt.decode(token, key, algorithms=['RS256'], audience=APP_ID, issuer='https://chat.cherry.fun')` with `PyJWKClient('https://chat.cherry.fun/.well-known/jwks.json')`, then require `app_id == APP_ID`; Go `github.com/MicahParks/keyfunc` + `golang-jwt` with the same checks.

## 5. Use the wallet

The Cherry wallet is already connected. With wallet-adapter, register `new CherryWalletAdapter()` (from `@cherrydotfun/miniapp-sdk/solana`) and enable `autoConnect`; with @solana/kit use `createCherrySigner(app)`.

- Before every signature, show what the transaction does and how much it moves.
- Label every transaction: one line in the app's words that Cherry's wallet sheet shows under the app's name, next to the amount Cherry decodes itself. With the SDK's wallet, `cherry.wallet.signAndSendTransaction(tx, { label: 'Buy 3 lives' })` (`signTransaction` / `signAllTransactions` take the same option); with wallet-adapter or a kit signer, wrap the call: `await withTransactionLabel('Buy 3 lives', () => sendTransaction(tx, connection))`. Name the action and the thing ("Swap 1 SOL to USDC", "Claim winnings"), at most 80 characters, never an amount different from what the transaction moves.
- Build for the wallet that pays: `cherry.paymentWallet` when it is set, otherwise the connected wallet. On `WALLET_CHANGED` or `NOT_A_SIGNER`, rebuild the transaction for the new wallet.
- Trust tier **unverified**: keep each transaction under $50 of outflow and expect at most $50 per wallet per day. Never request token approvals and delegation, authority changes, durable-nonce (delayed) transactions, recurring subscriptions.
- Handle refusals from the host and show a clear message, never retry in a loop:
  - `USER_REJECTED`: the user declined.
  - `POLICY_DENIED` with `err.policyCode` `TX_LIMIT`, `DAILY_LIMIT`, `FORBIDDEN_INSTRUCTION`, `APP_PAUSED`, `SIMULATION_FAILED` or `PRICE_UNAVAILABLE` (typed details in `err.policy`: `outflowUsd`, `perTxLimitUsd`, `dailyUsedUsd`, `dailyLimitUsd`): Cherry's limits stopped it; explain and offer a smaller amount where that makes sense. `isPolicyDenied(err)` from the SDK root narrows it.
  - `PRECHECK_UNAVAILABLE`: temporary; ask the user to try again.

## 6. Monetization

Nothing to build for fees. Do not send Cherry anything inside the app's transactions and do not call any billing API.

Cherry takes 10% of what the app earns: other (5% of Pump.fun creator fees on coins launched through the app, split on-chain at launch via Pump fee sharing. Users keep 95%. We take no cut of the SOL users spend in the app.): no share of volume declared; the developer states the revenue on the monthly bill. It measures the volume users move through the app itself (from the reference key in section 7 and its own wallet), and on the 1st it bills the developer for the previous month on the portal's Billing page, in USDC. Under $100 of volume a month there is no bill. If a bill is wrong (for example because the app's revenue does not follow volume), the developer enters the right amount with a reason and pays that.

Never add a hidden spread; every fee the app charges users is shown to them before they sign.

## 7. Attribute every transaction

Append the app reference key to one instruction of every transaction you ask the user to sign. It is a read-only, non-signer account derived from the app id, so Cherry and Dune can attribute volume and fees to this app on-chain.

```ts
import { getAppReferenceKey, withAppReference } from '@cherrydotfun/miniapp-sdk/solana';
const ix = withAppReference(myInstruction, '52e41534-4c7b-4237-9a16-ec8ea7a3c9dc');
// getAppReferenceKey('52e41534-4c7b-4237-9a16-ec8ea7a3c9dc') returns the PublicKey if you build instructions yourself.
```

## 8. Look native, speak their language, know who they are

- Mobile first: lay out for 360 px wide, no horizontal scroll, touch targets of at least 44 px.
- Language and theme: read `useCherryDisplayContext()` (`locale`, `colorScheme`, `safeArea`; known on the first frame from the `cherry_lang` / `cherry_theme` URL params, then live). Translate the UI into `locale` when you support it, follow `colorScheme` (dark is the default), pad by `safeArea` (fall back to `env(safe-area-inset-*)`). `applyCherryContextToDocument(context)` sets `<html lang>` and `data-cherry-theme` for CSS.
- Who they are: `useCherryUser()` is the person's public Cherry profile (display name, avatar, `@handle`, level, pet, socials, public wallets, badges, follower counts). Greet them by name with their avatar instead of a raw address; never show anything as private that the profile marks public, and never ask for what it already gives you.
- Social: `cherry.users.followers(cherryId)`, `.following(cherryId)` and `.relationship(cherryId)` (paged, launch token) power friend leaderboards and invites. A backend reads the same API with the token it verified (`GET https://chat.cherry.fun/api/miniapp/me`); it never takes a profile from the browser.
- Open Cherry profiles and rooms with `useCherryNavigate()` (`navigate.userProfile`, `navigate.openRoom`) instead of external links.

## 9. Legal pages and what the app must do

Link the Terms of Service (https://portal.cherry.fun/legal/app_b22266243fde/52e41534-4c7b-4237-9a16-ec8ea7a3c9dc/terms) and Privacy Policy (https://portal.cherry.fun/legal/app_b22266243fde/52e41534-4c7b-4237-9a16-ec8ea7a3c9dc/privacy) in the app footer or settings. Cherry hosts them for this app, generated from its listing: link them, do not copy them.

The developer accepted these duties in the Cherry Developer Agreement; build them in:

- Before every signature, say what the transaction does and how much it moves.
- Block the countries the app does not serve (CU, IR, KP) inside the app too, not only in the listing.
- If any content needs an 18+ rating, keep it behind the listing's 18+ rating.
- Users reach the developer through the app's page in Cherry; reports about the app are acted on within 72 hours.

## 10. Self-check before you report done

- [ ] Every address you deploy to loads over https, and every HTML response carries the frame-ancestors header from section 2 with no `X-Frame-Options`.
- [ ] Inside Cherry the app shows the signed-in user without a connect button or a signature request. (You cannot open the app inside Cherry from here: the listing wizard's automated test checks this and the frame.)
- [ ] `/.well-known/cherry-app.json` answers 200 with `{"appId": "52e41534-4c7b-4237-9a16-ec8ea7a3c9dc"}` on every origin of the app.
- [ ] Users are keyed by the Cherry ID (`cherry_id ?? sub`), not by the wallet.
- [ ] Every transaction carries a label (section 5).
- [ ] The backend rejects a token with the wrong `aud`, wrong issuer or expired `exp`.
- [ ] Every transaction carries the reference key.
- [ ] `POLICY_DENIED` and `USER_REJECTED` show a clear message.
- [ ] Terms of Service and Privacy Policy are linked inside the app.
- [ ] The layout works at 360 px wide in the dark theme.

When all boxes are ticked, tell the developer to open the Cherry Developer Portal, run the checks in the listing wizard and press Go live.
